about: Which reference judges each property of each setting of the plain GML specimen sheets (the GML draft's keys, no Creator), read by graphty-element/test/fidelity/oracle/judges.ts. No one program draws all of the draft's keys, so each property of each setting is judged by the first that draws it as the draft means: the sheet's oracle (OGDF 2025.10, oracles/<sample>.svg), else a stand-in (oracles/stand-ins/<sample>.<route>.svg), else the draft itself (a 'specification' rule: the expected drawing written over the oracle's, with the section it comes from), else no one ('none', with why). A property of a setting no rule names is the oracle's; common rules come before each sheet's, and a later rule overrides an earlier one. Settings are the specimens' ids (an edge's, its arrows' and its label's are the edge specimen's); '*' is every element. Chosen by what each program drew of each setting (the report's references), never by what graphty draws.

references.oracle: OGDF 2025.10, GraphIO::readGML and GraphIO::drawSVG of the sheet (route ogdf-draw): reads x, y, w, h, #RGB and #RRGGBB colors, type rectangle, Line, arrow and label
references.cytoscape-gml: Cytoscape desktop 3.10.5's GML reader (a stand-in): reads Tk's color names, width as a border or line width, and its own shape names only; names a node with no label by its id
references.gml2gv: Graphviz 14.1.2's gml2gv | neato -n2 (a stand-in): reads type as a Graphviz shape (oval an ellipse), width as the pen width, decodes GML's entities; draws fill as the outline color and every Line as a spline
references.specification: Himsolt, 'GML: Graph Modelling Language', draft of 19 Dec 1996 (Graphlet manual), appendix A, and the Tk 8.6 manuals its graphics follow (A.4): not a program, each rule cites its section
references.none: nothing the file sets and nothing the draft defines: judged by no one, so no program's own default is scored as GML's

common.why: the file sets no background and the draft names none: each program's canvas color is its own
the draft names no font for a label (A.1 label is its text alone) and the sheets set none: each program draws its own default font

OGDF draws rectangle alone of the draft's types and Cytoscape's GML reader reads only its own shape names (an oval is its default round rectangle); gml2gv passes oval to Graphviz, which draws it as an ellipse
OGDF does not read the draft's width (every outline and line is 1 px); Cytoscape's GML reader draws it
nothing is set: no program draws the draft's own defaults (A.4: w and h 0, an edge width of 0.0), so each draws its own and none is GML's

rules.why: the draft lists these types (A.4 type) but a node holds only its box: an arc needs Tk's start and extent, a line and a polygon their points, and a text item has no body; no program here draws them as Tk would, and the draft gives no drawing to expect

rules.source: Himsolt, 'GML: Graph Modelling Language', draft of 19 Dec 1996 (Graphlet manual), A.4 image ('the image is scaled to fit into the given dimensions') and bitmap ('used to draw an object'): the picture, a rectangle, draws the node
rules.why: no program here reads image or bitmap: OGDF and gml2gv draw a box with an outline, Cytoscape its round rectangle

rules.source: Himsolt, 'GML: Graph Modelling Language', draft of 19 Dec 1996 (Graphlet manual), A.4 image and bitmap (the picture draws the object), and the Tk 8.6 canvas manual (https://www.tcl.tk/man/tcl8.6/TkCmd/canvas.htm), whose graphics the draft's are 'modelled after' (A.4) (an image or bitmap item has no outline)
rules.why: no program here reads image or bitmap: each draws the node's outline around a plain box
the picture covers the node, and the comparator measures no picture's content (a picture graphty draws is only excused as a stray where the program draws one)
OGDF reads a color only as #RGB or #RRGGBB and draws a name black; Cytoscape's GML reader reads Tk's color names

rules.source: Tk_GetColor (https://www.tcl.tk/man/tcl8.6/TkLib/GetColor.htm): #RRRGGGBBB and #RRRRGGGGBBBB give each component in 3 or 4 hex digits, so #FFF888000 and #FFFF88880000 are #FF8800; the draft's colors are Tk's (A.4)
rules.why: no program here reads Tk's 9- and 12-digit colors: OGDF draws black, Cytoscape its default, gml2gv #ffff88 or no node

rules.source: Tk_GetColor: a color may be any name in Tk's color table, where 'light blue' is LightBlue, 173 216 230 (#ADD8E6); the draft's colors are Tk's (A.4)
rules.why: no program here reads a color name with a space: OGDF and gml2gv draw black, Cytoscape its default
OGDF draws a color name black; Cytoscape's GML reader reads it

a node's outer size depends on its outline: OGDF draws every outline 1 px wide and Cytoscape draws its border inside the box; gml2gv draws the outline as wide as width, centered on the box, as Tk does

rules.source: the Tk 8.6 canvas manual (https://www.tcl.tk/man/tcl8.6/TkCmd/canvas.htm), whose graphics the draft's are 'modelled after' (A.4): an item's outline is at least one pixel wide (an X11 line of width 0 is a thin line one pixel wide); the draft's width is Tk's (A.4)
rules.why: OGDF draws every outline 1 px wide whatever width says, Cytoscape draws none, and gml2gv's node is lost
OGDF reads a Tk stipple as one of its stroke types, which no Tk name is, and draws no outline; Cytoscape's GML reader ignores stipple and draws the outline

rules.source: Himsolt, 'GML: Graph Modelling Language', draft of 19 Dec 1996 (Graphlet manual), A.4 stipple, and the Tk 8.6 canvas manual (https://www.tcl.tk/man/tcl8.6/TkCmd/canvas.htm), whose graphics the draft's are 'modelled after' (A.4) -stipple (the fill is drawn through the bitmap: where a bit is off nothing is drawn); Tk_GetBitmap (https://www.tcl.tk/man/tcl8.6/TkLib/GetBitmap.htm): gray75, gray50, gray25 and gray12 are 75, 50, 25 and 12.5 percent gray
rules.why: no program here draws a stipple: OGDF, Cytoscape and gml2gv draw the fill whole

rules.source: the Tk 8.6 canvas manual (https://www.tcl.tk/man/tcl8.6/TkCmd/canvas.htm), whose graphics the draft's are 'modelled after' (A.4) -arrowshape (default {8 10 3}: the trailing points 10 back from the tip and 3 out from the line's edges, so 7.5 across a line 1.5 wide); the draft's arrow is Tk's (A.4)
rules.why: the file sets no arrowshape, so the arrowhead is Tk's default; OGDF draws its own, three times its 1 px line long

rules.source: the Tk 8.6 canvas manual (https://www.tcl.tk/man/tcl8.6/TkCmd/canvas.htm), whose graphics the draft's are 'modelled after' (A.4) line -smooth 1: the line is drawn as parabolic splines, one for each two segments, from the first point to the last (tkTrig.c TkMakeBezierCurve)
rules.why: OGDF ignores smooth and draws the Line straight, Cytoscape ignores the Line, gml2gv draws every Line as a spline
